# Flocks, herds and schools

The first particle model of flocking: each bird steers by three local rules, and no bird sees
the whole flock.

- Separation: avoid crowding nearby neighbours.
- Alignment: steer towards the average heading of neighbours.
- Cohesion: steer towards the average position of neighbours.

The model is purely local, yet the flock holds together and turns as one. That is the point I
keep coming back to: global order from local rules, with no leader and no shared plan.
